title: Testis
junior: The testes are the male reproductive glands. From puberty they make sperm cells and the hormone testosterone.
definition: The testes are the primary male sex organs, situated outside the abdominal cavity within a pouch called the scrotum.
structure: Each adult testis is oval, 4–5 cm long and 2–3 cm wide.
About 250 compartments called testicular lobules, each with one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules.
Seminiferous tubules are lined by male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells.
Interstitial spaces outside the tubules contain blood vessels and interstitial (Leydig) cells, and other immunologically competent cells.
functions: Leydig cells synthesise and secrete androgens (testosterone).
neetPoints: The scrotum keeps the testes 2–2.5 °C lower than the normal internal body temperature, which is necessary for spermatogenesis.
Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.
Spermatogenesis starts at puberty due to increased GnRH; LH acts on Leydig cells (androgens) and FSH on Sertoli cells (factors that help spermiogenesis).
commonMistakes: Leydig cells lie outside the seminiferous tubules; Sertoli cells lie inside them.

mcqs.explanation: Leydig cells in the interstitial spaces secrete androgens.

mcqs.stem: FSH acts on which cells of the testis?
mcqs.explanation: FSH acts on Sertoli cells; LH acts on Leydig cells.

title: Epididymis
junior: The epididymis is a coiled tube on the back of each testis where sperm cells are stored and mature.
definition: The epididymis is a coiled duct located along the posterior surface of each testis; it receives sperms from the vasa efferentia.
structure: Seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens.
functions: Stores sperms and helps them mature.
Transports sperms to the vas deferens.
neetPoints: Male accessory ducts: rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens.

mcqs.stem: The correct sequence of the male accessory ducts is:
options: Vasa efferentia → rete testis → epididymis → vas deferens
Rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens
Epididymis → rete testis → vas deferens → vasa efferentia
Rete testis → epididymis → vasa efferentia → vas deferens
mcqs.explanation: Seminiferous tubules open into vasa efferentia through the rete testis; these lead into the epididymis and then the vas deferens.

mcqs.stem: The epididymis is located along the:
mcqs.explanation: NCERT: epididymis is located along the posterior surface of each testis.

title: Seminal vesicles
junior: The seminal vesicles are two small glands behind the bladder. Their fluid gives sperm cells energy to swim.
definition: The seminal vesicles are paired male accessory glands; the duct of each joins the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.
structure: Coiled sac-like glands behind the urinary bladder.
functions: Secretion forms part of the seminal plasma, rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.
neetPoints: Male accessory glands: paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands.
Fructose in seminal plasma is the energy source for sperms.

mcqs.explanation: NCERT: the secretions of the male accessory glands are rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.

mcqs.stem: The vas deferens receives a duct from the seminal vesicle and opens into the urethra as the:
mcqs.explanation: Together they form the ejaculatory duct.

title: Prostate gland
junior: The prostate is a walnut-sized gland under the bladder that adds fluid to semen.
definition: The prostate is a single male accessory gland surrounding the urethra just below the urinary bladder.
structure: Glandular tissue with smooth muscle; the urethra and ejaculatory ducts pass through it.
neetPoints: Only the prostate is unpaired among the male accessory glands.

mcqs.stem: Which male accessory gland is unpaired?
mcqs.explanation: There are paired seminal vesicles, a single prostate and paired bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands.

mcqs.stem: Secretions of the bulbourethral glands help in:
mcqs.explanation: NCERT: bulbourethral secretions also help in the lubrication of the penis.

title: Penis
junior: The penis is the male external organ through which urine leaves the body.
definition: The penis is the male external genitalia; it is made up of special tissue that helps in erection to facilitate insemination.
structure: Corpora cavernosa (paired) and corpus spongiosum (surrounding the urethra).
Enlarged end = glans penis, covered by a loose fold of skin called the foreskin.
functions: Passage of urine and semen through the urethra.
neetPoints: The urethra extends through the penis to its external opening, the urethral meatus.

mcqs.stem: The urethra in males passes through the:
mcqs.explanation: The corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra.

mcqs.stem: The enlarged end of the penis is called the:
mcqs.explanation: It is covered by a loose fold of skin called the foreskin.
